summary: Community theaters across the region are launching workshops and training programs from September 2023 onward to discover and nurture local talent of all ages. Offerings span acting, technical theater, diversity initiatives, marketing, improv, playwriting, one-act plays and dance, each led by experienced professionals. The note stresses education, diversity, accessibility and mentorship as core values.
one_line: Community theaters are launching workshops from September 2023 in acting, tech, marketing, improv, playwriting, one-acts and dance to nurture local talent.
key_facts: The Evergreen Playhouse starts classes on September 10th, ranging from 'Introduction to Acting' for children to 'Advanced Scene Study' for adults.
Monica Stevens is artistic director of The Evergreen Playhouse and says the workshops are about 'instilling confidence, teamwork, and a deep appreciation for the arts.'
The Riverbank Theater Workshop begins October 5th as a comprehensive six-month program covering vocal techniques to set design, with veteran actor Jonathan Hughes among the instructors.
The Harmony Hall Arts Center's 'Diversity in Action' series rolls out in November, led by diversity advocate and director Sara Gilbert, to promote underrepresented voices.
A technical training workshop at the Midtown Cultural Center is set for late September, covering lighting, sound, costume and makeup with technician Alex Carter.
The 'Marketing Mastery for Theatrical Arts' workshop begins September 15th at the Liberty Arts Center, led by Emily Nguyen, teaching digital promotion tools.
Quirky Ques Theater offers 'Improv Weekends' starting October 21st under David Reynolds.
The annual 'Page to Stage' playwriting event starts December 1st, with veteran playwright Laura Fisher mentoring writers on character development, plot pacing and dialogue.
Grand Oak Theater's one-act play intensive workshop begins January 13th, led by Richard Stone, who calls one-act plays 'the sprint of the theater world.'
Alderwood Community Playhouse's 'Rhythms of Theater' dance series begins February 7th, curated by choreographer and dancer Anita Gonzalez.
Each workshop mentioned offers mentors through personalized coaching, group sessions or after-class consultations.
